name: Grilled eggplant with coconut milk
assumptions: Yield estimated from typical Filipino side-dish portions using 6 medium eggplants (about 4 servings as a light lunch/dinner accompaniment)
Total time estimated from grilling (~15-20 min), cooling/peeling (~5 min), and sauce/mixing (~5 min); no exact times given
Lemon powder in instructions treated as lemon juice per listed ingredient
Onions interpreted as green onions/scallions per instructions and 'sticks' measurement
All ingredients plant-based with no animal products
No gluten-containing ingredients listed or implied
No dairy, eggs, fish, shellfish, peanuts, wheat, soy, or sesame listed
Tree nuts left null due to possible cross-contamination ambiguity in coconut products despite no explicit tree nuts
instructions:
.  Prepare the eggplants for grilling by pricking them all over with a fork.  This is so it won’t burst during the grilling process as the natural water in it heats up.
2.  Grill the eggplants, turning them over frequently to ensure even cooking.  Grill until the skins are dark brown, even black and the eggplant is soft when you touch it.
3.  Soak the grilled eggplant in a bowl of water to cool it down.  Peel the skin off the eggplant.  Place the whole eggplants in a shallow dish (my mom actually cuts the eggplant into small, bite-sized pieces).
 4.  In a small mixing bowl, mix together the coconut milk or cream, lemon powder, salt and hot pepper.  Mix until the lemon powder and salt dissolve.  Taste, then adjust the amount of lemon powder, salt and hot pepper to your liking.  Pour the mixture over the eggplant.  Sprinkle the green onions over the eggplant and coconut milk.  Stir gently to combine.

ingredients.name: Egg Plants
ingredients.assumptions: 6 medium eggplants (about 200g each raw, edible portion after peeling and discarding skin ~198g each); typical size for grilling recipes

ingredients.name: Coconut Milk
ingredients.assumptions: 1 standard 400ml/13.5oz can of full-fat coconut milk; entire contents used

ingredients.name: Lemon Juice
ingredients.assumptions: 1 tablespoon bottled or fresh lemon juice (15ml by volume); 'lemon powder' in instructions interpreted as lemon juice per listed ingredient

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.assumptions: 1 teaspoon table salt; negligible calories and macros

ingredients.name: Red Pepper Flakes
ingredients.assumptions: 'To taste' red pepper flakes assumed as 2g (about 1 tsp) typical addition for a recipe of this size; common household amount for heat

ingredients.name: Onions
ingredients.assumptions: 4 sticks green onions/scallions (about 15g each raw, whole edible portion); common size in Filipino recipes, consistent with 'green onions' and 'sticks'
